script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination 2026. English Language Paper 3. Listening and Integrated Skills.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: The entire broadcast will last approximately one hour. During the examination, you will hear several recordings. You will have time to read the instructions and the questions. You will also have time to check your work.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Part A. Task 1. You are at the reception desk for the RestFest Urban Summit. You will hear a conversation between a staff member and a speaker. Complete the registration form below. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Good morning! Welcome to the RestFest Urban Summit 2026. We are expecting a huge crowd today—nearly two thousand attendees from across the globe. How can I help you with your registration today?

script.speaker: Julianne
script.text: Hello! I'm here to pick up the speaker credentials for my team. My name is Julianne Kwok. I'm with the Urban Harmony Institute. Have you got us on your list?

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Let me see... Urban Harmony... Ah, yes, here it is. Julianne Kwok, Urban Harmony Institute. Your mobile contact is 6288 1992. Is that correct?

script.speaker: Julianne
script.text: Yes, 6288 1992. And my keynote topic is 'Reclaiming Third Places'. I have a group of 8 members with me today.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Eight members. Noted. I see you've requested a holographic projector for your presentation. Is that still needed?

script.speaker: Julianne
script.text: Yes, definitely. The holographic projector is essential for our visual demonstration. And just to confirm, my lunch preference is nut-free and vegan.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Nut-free and vegan. I've updated the kitchen. Your workshop room is Zen Studio 4. Post-event networking is confirmed, and your transportation mode is the electric shuttle. Your payment reference is UH-REF-902.

script.speaker: Julianne
script.text: Perfect. And my emergency contact is Marcus Teo. His number is on file.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Marcus Teo. Confirmed. You're all set, Ms. Kwok. Enjoy the summit!

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 2. You will hear a talk by Professor Alan Mak on 'Third Places in Hong Kong'. Listen to the presentation and complete the notes below. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Prof Mak
script.text: Good morning, everyone. The term 'Third Place' was first coined by the American sociologist Ray Oldenburg in 1989. In his framework, the First Place is our home—the domestic space. The Second Place is our workplace or office. But the Third Place is where community happens—where social equality is the norm, regardless of your income or status.

script.speaker: Prof Mak
script.text: In Hong Kong, the biggest threat to third places is high rent. Traditional third places like the Dai Pai Dong are disappearing. Meanwhile, shopping malls have become pseudo-third places—they look public but are privately controlled and designed for consumption, not community.

script.speaker: Prof Mak
script.text: Our recent survey shows that 78% of the public wants more parks and free seating. We need 2,400 new benches across the city. I recommend Community Land Trusts as a policy solution. Our pilot district is Sham Shui Po. My next research publication will be released on October 12. Thank you.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 3. You will hear a panel of three experts debating the proposed 'Right to Disconnect' law. Listen to the discussion and tick the correct boxes in the table. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Welcome to our labour reform panel. Joining us are Dr. Wong, Ms. Beatrice Lam, and Mr. Felix Ho. Dr. Wong, should the law apply to all companies?

script.speaker: Dr Wong
script.text: Absolutely. The law must apply to all companies, not just SMEs or tech giants. No exceptions. The French model from 2017 proves this works.

script.speaker: Beatrice
script.text: I support the spirit, but I'm concerned about productivity loss. If workers truly disconnect, will output suffer? We need a 12-month grace period for implementation.

script.speaker: Felix
script.text: I agree with the 12-month grace period. But the current average overtime is 14 hours weekly—that's unsustainable. The penalty for after-hours emails should be a $50,000 fine. Public support is at 62%.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: What about exceptions?

script.speaker: Dr Wong
script.text: Only emergency services should be exempt. And we should promote the RestEasy HK wellness app to help workers transition.

script.speaker: Beatrice
script.text: Contact the labour union at rights@hkwu.org for details. The seminar continues in Exhibition Hall A.

script.speaker: Felix
script.text: And don't forget the official hashtag: #UnplugHK.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 4. You will hear three stakeholders discussing the 'Slow Living District' proposal for North Point. Listen to their conversation and complete the matrix below. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Today we're joined by a Local Shop Owner, a Young Professional, and an Urban Planner. Let's discuss the Slow Living District. Shop Owner, what's your main concern?

script.speaker: Shop Owner
script.text: Pedestrianisation means lost foot traffic. I want subsidised rent for artisanal shops. Maybe a weekend-only slow zone would be a good compromise.

script.speaker: Young Professional
script.text: I love the idea, but I need high-speed Wi-Fi even in slow zones. I'd love outdoor co-working spaces. And quiet booths in public parks would be amazing for calls.

script.speaker: Planner
script.text: My main concern is integration with existing MTR lines. The benefit would be a reduced urban heat island effect. I suggest vertical greening on highway pillars.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Can we reach consensus?

script.speaker: Planner
script.text: Let's set a 15 km/h speed limit for all vehicles in the pilot zone.

script.speaker: Shop Owner
script.text: Agreed, if the pilot launches in January 2027.

script.speaker: Young Professional
script.text: And the next public hearing should be at the Community Center on August 5.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: That is the end of Part A. You now have five minutes to study the Part B Question-Answer Book and the Data File. (300-second pause)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Integrated Skills Recording. You will now hear a briefing from the Director of Urban Harmony, Janice Wong, to the Project Manager regarding the upcoming tasks. Listen carefully and take notes as you will need this information to complete the tasks in Part B.

script.speaker: Janice
script.text: Good morning. I'm glad we're finally getting started on these tasks. We have a lot to do before the Q4 rollout. When you write that letter to the Shop Owners' Association for Task 8, please don't just repeat the brochure points. Emphasise that we aren't just creating 'wellness' jobs for yoga instructors. Mention that we are specifically looking to hire people with 'retail experience' and 'community outreach skills' to bridge the gap between slow-living concepts and local businesses. That's a key detail not in the Data File yet.

script.speaker: Janice
script.text: Moving on to the internal memo for Task 9—don't just list the budget gap. Propose a specific 'Wellness Weekend' in November to fix the publicity issue. We need to get local lifestyle influencers involved to build trust. And for the public social media post in Task 10, make sure to use a friendly, non-corporate tone. Use the phrase 'Breathe Easy HK' and make it sound like a neighbour talking to a neighbour.

script.speaker: Janice
script.text: One last thing—I just heard from the Urban Renewal Authority. They are very insistent that we describe our noise reduction technology as 'Whisper Quiet'. That's the specific term they want us to use in our responses to citizens like Ms. Clara Lam. 'Whisper Quiet'. Got it? Good. I expect those drafts on my desk by the end of the day. Good luck.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: That is the end of the Integrated Skills recording. You now have 1 hour and 10 minutes to complete your tasks. Stop writing when you hear the signal at the end of the examination.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (4200-second pause)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Stop writing now. The examination is over. Please stay in your seats until your scripts have been collected.

data_file.title: Minutes of the Urban Rest Bureau Planning Meeting
data_file.content:
Date: May 12, 2026. Attendees: Director Lo, PM Sarah Ho.
Discussion: Public dissatisfaction with 'always-on' work culture. Data shows 70% of workers feel burned out.
Action: Proposal for a 'Slow Living' certification for offices.
Note: Need to highlight that rest improves long-term productivity (Doc 9).

data_file.title: RestFest 2026: Official Program
data_file.content:
Theme: The Right to Rest.
Key Events:
- 'Unplugged' Yoga in Victoria Park.
- 'Digital Sabbath' workshop.
- Launch of 'Third Place' community cafes.
Slogan: 'Slow Down to Go Fast'.

data_file.title: Email from Clara Lam (Exhausted Citizen)
data_file.content:
To: Urban Rest Bureau.
I am a junior accountant. I get WhatsApp messages from my boss at 11 PM every night. I feel I have no 'Third Place' to go to. Even the local park is too loud with traffic. Please, we need laws to protect our rest time!

data_file.title: Editorial: The Vanishing Bench
data_file.content: HK Daily News: Public seating has decreased by 30% in the last decade. Why are we removing benches? To prevent 'loitering'? We are turning our city into a corridor, not a home. We need more 'Third Places' that are free to use.

data_file.title: Urgent Note from Director Janice Wong (Post-it Note)
data_file.content:
To: Project Manager

Just saw Clara Lam's email (Doc 3). We MUST reply to her. Be firm but polite. Explain that the 'Slow Living' certification is coming. Also, mention the RestEasy HK app features. We can't afford negative press right now. Also, for the internal memo (Task 9), make sure you mention we are hiring 100 'Wellness Ambassadors' to show we are creating jobs!

data_file.title: Viral Post from #SlowHK
data_file.content: Why is it that in HK, 'resting' is seen as 'laziness'? In Europe, they have the right to disconnect. We just have the right to more coffee and more work. #RightToRest #ThirdPlaceHK

data_file.title: Internal Memo: 'Right to Disconnect' Pilot
data_file.content: To all staff: From June 1st, we are trialing 'No-Email Weekends'. Unless it's a Grade-1 Emergency, staff are not expected to check servers or reply to messages until Monday 9 AM.

data_file.title: Research: The Science of Rest
data_file.content: A 10-minute micro-break increases focus by 25%. Access to 'Third Places' reduces cortisol levels by 15%. Overworking leads to a 40% increase in errors in financial reporting.

data_file.title: Draft Section: Slow Living District Zoning
data_file.content: Clause 2.3: All new commercial developments in designated Slow Living Districts must allocate 15% of ground floor space for free public seating or community cafes. Noise levels must not exceed 55 decibels after 8:00 PM.
